headline: Granted a development permit for a 511 Maine Avenue training center and a new lot at 6 Bangor Mall Boulevard.
summary: Granted a Land Development Permit for a 6,070 sq. ft. training center and restoration of a cold storage building at 511 Maine Avenue. Granted a Minor Subdivision Modification and Planned Group Development creating a 0.54-acre and a 6.24-acre lot at 6 Bangor Mall Boulevard. Discussed a proposed growth boundary change, downtown floor area ratio rules, and land use plan updates, with no votes taken.

# COMMUNITY & ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT

**CITY OF BANGOR**

PLANNING DIVISION

**PLANNING BOARD**

**TUESDAY, OCTOBER 6, 2026, 7:00 P.M.**

**COUNCIL CHAMBERS, 1ST FLOOR OF CITY HALL**

**73 HARLOW STREET**

## MEETING MINUTES

**Board Members Present:**

- Chair Jonathan Boucher
- Vice Chair Janet Jonas
- Ted Brush
- Trisha Hayes
- Ken Huhn
- Greg Hobson (via Zoom)
- Ross Whitford

**City Staff Present:**

- Anja Collette, Planning Officer
- Matt Altiero, Planning Analyst
- Grace Innis, Assistant City Solicitor
- Jefferson Davis, Engineering Director

Chair Boucher called the meeting to order at 7:00 P.M.

## OLD BUSINESS

1. **Meeting Minutes – September 1, 2026**

Member Huhn moved to approve the minutes of September 1, 2026. Seconded by Vice Chair Jonas. Roll call vote conducted – all voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed.

2. **Adopt Findings & Decisions for 201 Odlin Rd and 8-10 Harlow St**

Member Huhn moved to adopt the findings and decisions for 201 Odlin Road and 8-10 Harlow Street. Seconded by Member Brush. Roll call vote conducted – all voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed.

## NEW BUSINESS

1. **Land Development Permit Application – Major Site Development and Site Location of Development (SLODA) Modification – 511 Maine Avenue – Map-Lot 001-001-G – City of Bangor Community Connector** – Land Development Permit Application – Major Site Development and Site Location of Development (SLODA) Modification for the construction of a 6,070 sq. ft. training center and restoration of existing cold storage building, including drainage and stormwater improvements, new parking, and access drives located at 511 Maine Avenue, Map-Lot 001-001-G, in the Government & Institutional Service District (G&ISD). Applicant/Owner: City of Bangor Community Connector.

Chair Boucher introduced the agenda item.

Vice Chair Jonas moved that the Board finds the application was deemed complete on October 6th, 2026, all applicable fees for the project have been paid, and the proposed project is a Major Site Development and Site Location of Development (SLODA) modification. Seconded by Member Huhn. Roll call vote conducted – all voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed.

Applicant Representative Shelly Lizotte presented on the project, discussing the need for restoration. Lizotte presented on the training center expansion details.

Chair Boucher asked for questions or comments from staff – there were none.

Chair Boucher opened public comment – there were none. Public comment closed.

Chair Boucher asked the board for any questions or comments – there were none.

Member Huhn moved that the Board finds that, based on Exhibit 2, the applicant satisfied Land Development Code §165-33.1's requirements surrounding Erosion and Sediment Control. Seconded by Member Brush. Roll call vote conducted – all voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed.

Member Brush moved that the Board finds that, based on Exhibit 2, the applicant satisfied Land Development Code §165-68's requirements for lot frontage. Seconded by Member Hayes. Roll call vote conducted – all voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed.

Member Hayes moved that the Board finds that, based on Exhibits 2 and 16, the applicant satisfied Land Development Code §165-72 regarding the required number of parking spaces, §165-73's requirements regarding parking area location and screening, and §165-74's requirements regarding parking area design, construction, and maintenance. Seconded by Member Whitford. Roll call vote conducted – all voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed.

Member Brush moved that the Board finds that, based on Exhibits 2, 7, 13-15, 20, and 21, the applicant satisfied Land Development Code §165-79 requiring adequate utility service, including water, electricity, fire protection, and provision for stormwater runoff. Seconded by Vice Chair Jonas. Roll call vote conducted – all voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed.

Vice Chair Jonas moved that the Board finds that, based on Exhibits 2 and 21, the applicant satisfied Land Development Code §165-80 requiring that whenever possible, all uses and developments shall be provided with water service from the Bangor Water District. Seconded by Member Huhn. Roll call vote conducted – all voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed.

Member Huhn moved that the Board finds that, based on Exhibits 2 and 8, the applicant satisfied Land Development Code §165-81 requiring providing adequate lighting and preventing light pollution and trespass. Seconded by Member Hayes. Roll call vote conducted – all voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed.

Member Brush moved that the Board finds that, based on Exhibits 2 and 20, the applicant satisfied Land Development Code §165-82 requirements regarding having adequate fire protection. Seconded by Member Huhn. Roll call vote conducted – all voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed.

Member Hayes moved that the Board finds that, based on Exhibit 2, the applicant satisfied the Land Development Code §165-83 requiring adequate electrical services. Seconded by Member Huhn. Roll call vote conducted – all voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed.

Member Huhn moved that the Board finds that, based on Exhibits 2, 7, 13-15, and 21, the applicant satisfied the Land Development Code §165-84 requiring provisions for surface water and storm drainage. Seconded by Member Brush. Roll call vote conducted – all voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed.

Member Brush moved that the Board finds that, based on Exhibits 2 and 16, the applicant satisfied Land Development Code §165-114B's requirement that the proposed parking and loading layout are arranged in a reasonable and safe configuration and §165-114C's requirement that all proposed access drives are reasonably necessary and safe. Seconded by Member Huhn. Roll call vote conducted – all voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed.

Member Huhn moved that the Board finds that, based on Exhibit 2, the applicant satisfied Land Development Code §165-114C's requirement that all proposed access drives from the site to any public right-of-way are reasonably necessary and safe. Seconded by Vice Chair Jonas. Roll call vote conducted – all voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed.

2. **Land Development Permit Application – Minor Subdivision Modification and Planned Group Development – 6 Bangor Mall Boulevard – Map-Lot 061-016-A – Waterstone Bangor, LLC** – Land Development Permit Application – Minor Subdivision Modification and Planned Group Development for the creation of a 0.54-acre and 6.24-acre lot from an existing 6.78-acre parcel located at 6 Bangor Mall Boulevard, Map-Lot 061-016-A, in the Shopping & Personal Service District (S&PS). Applicant/Owner: Waterstone Bangor, LLC.

Chair Boucher introduced the agenda item.

Member Huhn moved that the Board finds the application was deemed complete on October 6th, 2026, all applicable fees for the project have been paid, and the proposed project is a Minor Subdivision Modification and Planned Group Development. Seconded by Member Brush. Roll call vote conducted – all voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed.

Applicant Representative Sean Thies presented on the project, discussing the creation of a new lot.

Chair Boucher asked for comments from staff – there were none.

Chair Boucher asked the Board for any questions.

Member Huhn asked if there is a purpose yet for the new parcel. Applicant Representative Thies responded that while there is discussion surrounding proposed development on the lot, nothing is finalized.

Vice Chair Jonas asked how the lot size was decided. Applicant Representative Thies responded it is based off a preliminary plan of what could go there, and it would be suitable for a variety of uses.

Chair Boucher opened public comment – there were none. Public comment closed.

Chair Boucher asked the Board if there is any discussion or additional questions – there were none.

Member Huhn moved that the Board finds that, based on Exhibits 2, 7, 8, and 9, the Project meets the requirements of Land Development Code §165-126F(1), regarding compliance with State of Maine guidelines for subdivision approval contained in 30-A M.R.S.A. §4404. Seconded by Member Brush. Roll call vote conducted – all voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed.

Member Huhn moved that the Board finds that, based on Exhibits 2 and 9, the Project meets the requirements of Land Development Code §165-126F(2) regarding conforming to the existing lot dimension and area regulations of the zoning district, §165-126F(3)'s requirement of abutting an existing improved public road, and §165-126F(4)'s requirement on the angle of side lot lines to street lines. Seconded by Member Brush. Roll call vote conducted – all voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed.

Vice Chair Jonas moved that the Board finds that, based on Exhibit 2, the Project meets the requirements of Land Development Code §165-126F(6), regarding the plat containing all information required in 165-126D(1-8). Seconded by Member Huhn. Roll call vote conducted – all voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed.

Member Brush moved that the Board finds that, based on Exhibit 2, the applicant satisfied §165-69 of the Land Development Code regarding the requirements for planned group developments. Seconded by Member Hayes. Roll call vote conducted – all voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed.

Member Huhn moved that the Board finds that the project meets the requirements for a Minor Subdivision Modification and Planned Group Development and therefore, the Board grants the Land Development Permit for the proposed Project. Seconded by Member Brush. Roll call vote conducted – all voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed.

## OTHER BUSINESS

Planning Officer Collette reminded Board members to lean forward into the microphone when speaking to ensure attendees on Zoom can hear what is being said. She asked the Board to spread the word about applying to Planning Board, as there will be two vacancies in the upcoming year. Collette asked whether the Board has any feedback on the way the packets are structured.

Member Whitford asked if there are two positions open plus the Associate Member, or two including the Associate Member. Planning Officer Collette responded that it was two including the Associate Member.

1. **Proposed Growth Boundary Change**

Chair Boucher introduced the agenda item.

Planning Officer Collette presented on the proposed growth boundary change, discussing how the access to water and sewer is compatible with the change. She discussed that the VA is interested in putting in a new VA hospital at the corner of Stillwater Avenue and Kittredge Road. Collette noted that existing development in the area contributed to the location choice. She explained the formal process with Planning Board, City Council, and the State. Collette discussed hosting a public workshop in advance of a formal meeting to discuss the proposal with abutters and receive their feedback.

Member Huhn expressed excitement about the prospect of a VA hospital.

Member Brush asked what the availability is of alternate sites for the potential project. Planning Officer Collette responded that the VA explored sites near the airport, but had concerns surrounding noise and proximity to the airport. Brush noted that there is not an abundance of alternate sites.

Vice Chair Jonas discussed that after doing a survey of Bangor for alternate sites, she did not identify an available alternate site. Jonas asked about sewer capacity – Planning Officer Collette responded that the VA is working with the sewer team to resolve any issues. Engineering Director Davis discussed a multi-phase project to increase sewer capacity in that area.

Member Brush asked about water capacity – Planning Officer Collette responded that the Bangor Water District has not expressed any water capacity concerns.

Chair Boucher asked whether staff is seeking conversation, or looking to see if there are any objections from the Board – Planning Officer Collette responded to see if there are objections. Boucher asked if anyone had any additional comments – there were none.

Planning Officer Collette shared that the public workshop is set to occur October 29th.

2. **Workshop on removing the floor area ratio restriction from Downtown Development District (DDD)**

Chair Boucher introduced the agenda item.

Planning Officer Collette presented on the proposed amendment, discussing how floor area ratio restrictions are outdated and may be difficult to understand. She discussed using design standards as an alternate way to control for building scale and form. Collette noted that the Business and Economic Development Committee expressed concerns surrounding the lack of height limits downtown, so

proposals for an overall height limit may emerge in later discussions. She explained that the floor area ratio is the total gross floor area of a building divided by the area of a lot.

Member Brush noted that he supports the effort to find alternative measures for protecting sunlight and building style or bulk of the building. Planning Officer Collette responded that it could be controlled for with building envelope standards. Vice Chair Jonas discussed that there are portions of downtown that receive little sun, especially in the winter, but is unsure if it is feasible to protect that. Jonas shared that she is in favor of making changes to promote more housing infill.

Chair Boucher asked if there is a way to include conditional use into this so the Board would still have grounds to discuss it. Planning Officer Collette asked if he is seeking for the current change to include a provision in for condition use. Boucher discussed picking a new floor area ratio number and including that anything above it is a conditional use. Collette discussed the alternative of selecting a preliminary height limit for that, and asked if there are concerns about other aspects of the floor area ratio. Boucher responded it may be nice to see examples of buildings that are currently not compliant to provide context. Collette noted two historic buildings nearby that exceed the limit.

Member Whitford expressed that he agrees with Vice Chair Jonas, and that the only way to develop for buildings downtown is to go up.

Planning Officer Collette noted that the Board is comfortable moving forward with the change, and to include more guardrails for building form with the Land Development Code updates. She shared that the Historic Preservation Commission has purview over much of downtown and building form.

### 3. Follow-Up/Thoughts on Land Use Plan Updates

Planning Officer Collette shared that the consultants anticipate review to be completed by mid-November and having a public draft out by early next year. She provided updates surrounding the zoning map and a potential airport overlay district.

Planning Officer Collette noted that there will not be a Planning Board meeting on Election Day

Meeting adjourned at 8:01 PM.

Respectfully submitted,

Kayleigh Rienas
Development Assistant
Planning Division
